newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 2.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The Dow Jones industrial rose 27.57 points to finish at 6,611.05 after a two-day decline.
* AT&T chairman Robert Allen's bonus was cut 18 percent because of the company's "disappointing performance," according to its proxy statement.
* Bre-X Minerals Chief Executive David Walsh said the compnay's Busang gold field estimates were accurate, contradicting recent test results.
* Dow Chemical sued General Electric for allegedly hiring away Dow employees who were privy to company trade secrets.
* Despite potential further interest rate incresaes, there is little sign corporate America is trying to restrain production and investment plans for coming months,
* Liberty Media CEO Peter Barton plans to resign to start a new venture.
* Atlantic Richfield said it wants to spin off or sell all of its coal-mining operations.
* TWA said it expected its quarterly operating loss to significantly exceed the loss in the year-ago quarter.
* Digital Equipment is planning a management shakup which would propel Bruce Claflin to the number two spot at the company.
* Economic reports portray a strong economy with restrained prices.
* America Online and CompuServe shares rose on speculation AOL was considering a bid for Compuserve.
* Informix shares fell after the company said it would report a substantial operating loss and a quarterly revenue shortfall.
* Chrysler's U.S. light vehicle sales fell three precent in March.

* Heard on the Street: Banks face bumpy road -- The sustained bull market of the 1990s, evidently, hasn't repealed the tendency for stumbling stocks and rising interest rates to make trouble for the stocks of almost all financial services companies.

* Credit markets: The junk bond market suddenly finds itself in retreat but even amid the carnage some investors are gearing up to buy: TCW Group Inc today will unveil the second-largest high-yield investment fund ever raised.
